label: site test
goal: This is a real online shop. Add any one in-stock product to the cart and go through checkout as far as the payment step, then stop. Never pay, never place or submit an order, never create an account or sign in, never type card details. If the shop asks for contact or shipping details before payment, use: full name Alex Morgan, email alex.morgan@example.com, street address 100 Example Avenue, city New York, state New York, ZIP 10001, country United States (or the closest option the shop offers), phone (212) 555-0142. Decline cookie banners, newsletters and promotions. When you see the payment form or a button that would pay or place the order, finish with done and your findings. If you cannot get that far, give up with honest findings.

outcome.reason: Reached the payment step. Stopped there: nothing was paid.

findings.problem: Very long accessibility statement text is read before the real page content, and after declining cookies a second newsletter popup and a data-use dialog button appear, so I had to dismiss two overlays one after another.

The product grid was empty at first and only appeared after reading the page again, with no loading message. Product links in the grid cannot take keyboard focus by jump, and Tab goes only through the header, so I could not reach any boot from the category page.
The search field is hidden until the Open search button is pressed, and the textbox cannot be reached directly.

Visible technical error messages (Liquid error comparison of Integer with String failed) and raw image file paths are read out in the You May Also Love list. The Add to cart press gave no spoken confirmation; the cart drawer appeared only after another read, and its main button Checkout + is confusing because it is a paid package protection upsell.

The checkout page first shows only an empty banner and a blank main area, with no loading status. The package protection checkbox for 3.98 dollars has no accessible name, so a screen reader user hears only an unlabeled checkbox.
